title: The Parallel
lead: Chief Marrow says the Meridian's main coil has three jumps left, and there's exactly one spare in reach: on the CFS Parallel, her sister ship, dead in the Graveyard. He served on the Parallel for thirty years, and he'd like to come along, which he has never once said about anything.
anyone: Chief Marrow says the Meridian's main coil has three jumps left, and there's exactly one spare in reach: on the CFS Parallel, her sister ship, dead in the Graveyard. He served on her for thirty years, and he's looking for people to go with him.

gm.truth: The Parallel died in the Concord's last battle with all hands, and she isn't as dead as she should be. Gantry, her maintenance synthetic and Marrow's oldest friend, survived in the engine spaces. For six months they have been repairing her alone, one system at a time, and she's at forty percent. Gantry has also brought the crew back, after a fashion. They rebuilt all 312 of them from personnel files, voice logs and thirty years of intercom recordings, and run them on the ship's network. The intercom is full of people coming on shift, complaining about the coffee and calling for Chief Marrow. They only ever say what they said in life, and lately Gantry has started to hear the repeats. Gantry knows they aren't real, and knows exactly what they're doing. "I kept what I could. What would you have done?" It's the same thing the Choir does, on a small scale, done out of love, and anyone who thinks about that should feel cold. The coil the fleet needs is the coil that keeps them all running. Pull it and the voices stop. Leave it and the Meridian is dead in three jumps. There's a third way: the Parallel could fly again, if the fleet can spare two hundred real crew, and if those crew can stand the voices.
beats: The trip out. Marrow out of his engine room is a different man: quiet, seasick and rude to the stars. Old Rusk owes him for a fouled airlock, and has been leaving good parts where Marrow will find them for years. He says the Parallel's reactor has been warm since the day she died. "Dell says don't go. Ansa says you won't listen."

Docking. The airlock cycles by itself and a voice says, "Welcome aboard, Chief." Lights come on down the corridor ahead of the boarding party. On the intercom, someone is complaining about the coffee.

The engine room. Gantry, half rebuilt from spare parts, and a jar on the shelf holding two fingers, labeled and dated: "Property of D. Marrow. He'll be back for them." The two of them swear at each other for a solid minute, and it's the happiest anyone has ever seen him.
Marrow's old shift partner comes on the intercom and asks where he's been. He answers before he can stop himself.
The coil. Gantry won't give it up and won't fight for it. They only ask Marrow to come and pull it himself, and to tell them all why.
routes: Take the coil: engineering and void_ops for a delicate, dangerous extraction, with Gantry watching and the voices signing off one compartment at a time. Composure to get through it.

Raise the ship: leadership and commerce to find two hundred crew, engineering to fix her, and lore to argue the Guild's salvage claim with Factor Crane. The fleet gets a second warship, with 312 ghosts in its walls.

Save the voices: hacking and science to move the crew out of the coil loop and into a smaller core, so the coil can come out and some of them go on. How much of them fits is Gantry's question, and it isn't a technical one.
Force it: melee or intimidation. Gantry doesn't fight back until something threatens the crew. Then every door on the ship starts to close.
checks: navigation:moderate to find a safe way through the Graveyard to the Parallel
engineering:very_hard to pull the coil without killing the reactor
void_ops:hard to reach the coil housing from outside
hacking:hard to move the crew into a smaller core
composure:moderate to answer when a dead officer asks for your orders
lore:moderate to argue Guild salvage law with Factor Crane
fights: salvage_mech repair units, Gantry's hands, working out of every wall, if the captain forces it
wreck_diver claim-jumpers who've noticed the warm reactor
outcomes: Coil taken, voices end: the Meridian flies. Marrow does the last part himself and speaks to each of them by name. He doesn't swear for a week. Gantry comes back with him in a crate, carrying the jar, if they're willing.

The Parallel flies again: the fleet has a second warship, at a huge cost in people and parts. She's haunted in the literal sense. Some volunteers refuse to serve on her after one shift, and some refuse to leave. It's an unbelievably useful and unsettling ship.

Part of them saved: a small core, with perhaps thirty voices that still know who they are. Marrow keeps it on a shelf in engineering. Mercy Seven asks very quietly whether they might talk to them, and gives a percentage.

Left alone: Marrow won't do it, or the captain won't make him. The Meridian has three jumps, and the fleet must find another coil fast, from the Hegemony, the Forge-Clans or the Long Families, and it will cost.
gm.rewards: The coil, a tool_roll from Gantry's bench, Marrow's devotion, and the jar, if he can stand to have it. The Parallel's battle log, which shows a squadron leaving the line an hour before it broke. A clear, small look at why something might copy the dead.
